title: India Approves Wegovy for Fatty Liver Disease in New Milestone for GLP-1 Drugs
excerpt: India's drug regulator has cleared Novo Nordisk's semaglutide injection for treating MASH, a serious form of fatty liver disease that affects roughly two in three Indians, making it the first GLP-1 drug approved for this condition both globally and in India.
body:
Key Takeaways
  • India's CDSCO approved Wegovy for treating MASH, a severe fatty liver disease.
  • Wegovy is the first GLP-1 drug approved for MASH globally and in India.
  • Approximately two in three Indians are affected by fatty liver disease.
  • The approval follows the U.S. FDA's clearance of Wegovy for MASH in August 2025.
  • Wegovy's market expansion faces competition from generics and other GLP-1 drugs.

  • India's CDSCO has approved Wegovy (semaglutide 2.4 mg) for noncirrhotic MASH with moderate to advanced liver fibrosis in adults.
  • Wegovy is the first and only GLP-1 receptor agonist approved both globally and in India for MASH treatment.
  • About two in three people in India have fatty liver disease, and MASH often progresses silently until severe damage occurs.
  • The approval follows the U.S. FDA's clearance of Wegovy for MASH in August 2025, based on the phase 3 ESSENCE trial.

CDSCO Greenlights Wegovy for Liver Disease

India's Central Drugs Standard Control Organisation (CDSCO) has approved a new indication for Novo Nordisk's Wegovy — the blockbuster weight-loss injection — to treat metabolic dysfunction-associated steatohepatitis (MASH), a severe form of fatty liver disease, the Danish drugmaker announced on Friday.

The approval covers Wegovy's 2.4 mg semaglutide injection for adults with noncirrhotic MASH and moderate to advanced liver fibrosis (stages F2 to F3), to be used alongside a reduced-calorie diet and increased physical activity. It makes Wegovy the first and only GLP-1 receptor agonist cleared for MASH treatment both in India and globally.

MASH, formerly known as nonalcoholic steatohepatitis (NASH), develops when excess fat builds up in the liver, triggering chronic inflammation and progressive scarring. Left untreated, it can advance to cirrhosis, liver failure, cancer, and the need for a transplant.

"At week 72, 63% of patients on semaglutide achieved resolution of steatohepatitis without worsening fibrosis, compared with 34% on placebo."

"This approval is an important milestone, giving doctors and patients a new option for people at risk of MASH while also helping to address obesity and related heart and metabolic diseases."

- Vikrant Shrotriya, Managing Director, Novo Nordisk India

India's Outsized Fatty Liver Burden

The approval comes as India grapples with a surging fatty liver epidemic tied to rising obesity, diabetes, and sedentary lifestyles. Novo Nordisk said about two in three people in India have fatty liver disease. A meta-analysis in the Journal of Clinical and Experimental Hepatology estimated that approximately one in three Indian adults have NAFLD, with prevalence reaching 52.8% among high-risk groups including those with obesity or diabetes.

Treatment options for MASH have been severely limited. Before Wegovy, the only FDA-approved MASH treatment was resmetirom (Rezdiffra), cleared in the U.S. in 2024, which works directly on liver cells. Semaglutide takes a different approach — suppressing appetite and promoting weight loss to reduce liver fat, inflammation, and fibrosis.

Clinical Evidence Behind the Approval

India's approval mirrors the U.S. FDA's clearance of Wegovy for MASH in August 2025, both based on the phase 3 ESSENCE trial. That study randomly assigned 1,197 patients to semaglutide 2.4 mg or placebo for 240 weeks. At week 72, 63% of patients on semaglutide achieved resolution of steatohepatitis without worsening fibrosis, compared with 34% on placebo. Additionally, 37% on semaglutide saw fibrosis improvement without worsening steatohepatitis, versus 22% on placebo.

The CDSCO's approval is conditional — Novo Nordisk must submit the complete clinical study report for Part 2 of the ESSENCE trial, a confirmatory study evaluating long-term endpoints including progression to cirrhosis, liver decompensation, transplant, and mortality.

Competitive Landscape in India's GLP-1 Market

Wegovy, already approved in India for chronic weight management since its launch in June 2025, has sold about 76,000 units in the first half of 2026, according to Pharmarack. The MASH indication could significantly expand its market.

But Novo Nordisk faces stiff competition. Eli Lilly's Mounjaro (tirzepatide) entered India first in March 2025. Meanwhile, semaglutide's Indian patent expired in March 2026, opening the door for generics. Sun Pharma's Noveltreat and Dr Reddy's generic semaglutide are already approved, priced well below Novo Nordisk's branded product. Wegovy's monthly cost ranges from about ₹17,345 for lower doses to ₹26,015 for the full 2.4 mg dose.

Implications for the Diaspora

South Asians are disproportionately susceptible to metabolic conditions including NAFLD and type 2 diabetes, even at lower body mass indices. Family members in India now have access to a MASH treatment previously available only in the U.S. and select markets. The availability of both branded Wegovy and upcoming generics could make treatment more accessible for diaspora members seeking affordable options during visits home. Novo Nordisk has said it is pursuing similar approvals in the European Union and Japan.
